h1: Does the grouped fish and bird picornavirus module work?
standfirst: PICO_NOLDR_VP0 groups five genera of fish, bird and seal picornaviruses that share one genome organisation: no leader, and a capsid left as VP0 rather than cleaved. None has enough sequence in BV-BRC to model alone. This audit is mostly about what that grouping does and does not buy, because the answer here is sharper than for any other module in the family.
lede01: Five genera, 68 near-complete genomes, and one of them supplies most of the data.
p01: Pasivirus (pig), Avisivirus and Limnipivirus (birds and fish), Potamipivirus (fish) and Aquamavirus (seal). The layout is shared: POLY, VP0, VP3, VP1, 2A, 2B, 2C, 3A, VPg, 3C, 3D.
Of the 53 near-complete exemplars, 29 are Pasivirus. Limnipivirus contributes 11, Avisivirus 8, Potamipivirus 3 and Aquamavirus 2. That imbalance is the whole story of this page.
lede02: Eleven features, 28 profiles. Aquamavirus fragments were dropped rather than modelled.
p02: Aquamavirus contributed 2C records of 15 residues and VP3 records of 40, against 330 and 230 for every other genus. Those are fragments, not short forms, and left in they would have dragged the 2C window floor to 12 and the VP3 floor to 32 — wide enough to admit a fragment of anything. They were dropped, so Aquamavirus is represented in the capsid and polymerase features and not in those two.
lede03: Windows at 0.8× to 1.2× the collection median; bit cutoffs at 0.45× the median length.
lede04: Fourteen rep contigs, and all 53 exemplars route.
p04: Routing is the part that works. Fourteen references reach every genome in all five genera, which is what shared genome organisation delivers: the nucleotide-level similarity is enough to assign a genome to the module.
lede05: Pasivirus gets everything. The other four genera get the polyprotein and little else.
p05:
This is the measurement that matters and it is stark:

Pasivirus is called on 29 of 29 for every one of the eleven features. The other 24 exemplars get the polyprotein in most cases, 3D in about half, and almost nothing else.
p06: The panel is drawn round-robin across species, so it is dominated by Pasivirus in the same proportion as the genus holdings. A high clean rate here is not evidence that the module works for the other four genera.
lede07: Shared organisation routes a genome. It does not give you a profile.
p07: For seven of the eleven features, only Pasivirus contributed a cluster at all. VP0, VP3, 2A, 2C, 3A, VPg and 3C are each built from Pasivirus sequences and nothing else. VP1 and 2B add Aquamavirus, 3D adds Limnipivirus, and POLY — the longest and most conserved feature — manages four of the five genera.

The cause is arithmetic, not divergence alone. Limnipivirus contributes 3 sequences to most collections, Avisivirus 3, Potamipivirus 3 and Aquamavirus 1. A profile needs at least two sequences from the same genus that are similar enough to cluster, and with one to three sequences apiece that condition usually fails. The documented member floor of five is unreachable; even the leftover pass, which drops the floor to two, cannot build from a single sequence.

This was diagnosed, a fix was attempted, and the fix did not work. The first build used the documented -m 5 throughout, which let only Pasivirus cluster. The module was rebuilt with the leftover pass at its floor of two, which is the sanctioned route to a small profile. The call rates moved by exactly one genome — POLY from 48 to 49. Reporting that is more useful than reporting the rebuild as an improvement, because it locates the limit precisely: the problem is not the floor, it is that four of these genera have one to three sequences per protein in the entire public record.

So what the module is, honestly, is a Pasivirus module that four other genera route to. That is still worth shipping — a genome that routes and gets its polyprotein called is better annotated than one that routes nowhere — but it should not be described as covering five genera. Closing the gap needs more sequence from those genera, not a parameter change.
verdict07: Routing works for all five genera; profiles work for one. Pasivirus is called completely, and the other four get the polyprotein and little else because they contribute one to three sequences per protein. A rebuild through the leftover pass changed the result by a single genome, which is the evidence that this is a data limit rather than a tuning one.
lede08: The run found that the grouping premise only half holds.
p08: Grouping by genome organisation is the project's partitioning rule, and it is right about what it claims: these five genera do share a layout, and the shared layout is enough for fourteen reference contigs to route all of them. What the rule does not promise, and what this module demonstrates, is that routing and calling are different problems. Profiles need sequence similarity within a feature, and organisation-sharing does not supply it.

The practical lesson for the next grouped module is to check, before building, how many sequences each genus contributes to each feature. A genus contributing fewer than two sequences to a feature cannot be covered by it, and knowing that in advance turns a disappointing coverage run into a declared limitation.
